135: Dennis Agerblad Band on Denmark's Got Talent
137: One day, a woman from Denmark's Got Talent called to ask whether Dennis Agerblad Band would like to take part in the programme.
138: I said no, but she kept trying to persuade me. I should think of it as publicity for my band. I explained that nobody watched the programme and that we were hardly a good fit for mainstream family TV. We mostly performed at underground venues. But they had seen my website and felt the programme needed people like us.
139: And that is how we ended up on Denmark's Got Talent.
146: After our audition, we were told that unfortunately we hadn't made it through. The others in the band were disappointed, but I knew this was how they made good television. Shortly afterwards, they called again and asked if they could send

243: Four authors have written the book they had always wanted to read. BØSSEDANMARK is a powerful collection of short stories about twenty different gay men's lives in twenty different places in Denmark. The book is published on 16 August 2021 during Copenhagen Pride. To mark its release, the authors will give a talk at Arnold Busck on Købmagergade on 15 August, from 2 to 4 pm. There will also be an open launch reception on 16 August at Bøssehuset in Christiania.
244: There are gay men everywhere in Denmark. Every little town has a few. Every block of flats. Every parish. From Copenhagen to Vester Skerninge. From Allinge to Hvide Sande.
